kind: systemic behavior closure contract (experimental; introduces no canonical owner)

taskSuccessIsNotSystemCorrectness.meaning: a benchmark or task PASS is a statement about a behavioural outcome, never about the mechanism that produced it
taskSuccessIsNotSystemCorrectness.consequence: no behavioural experiment may support a mechanism claim while SYSTEM_VALID is false

outcomeCannotRepairMechanism.statement: Outcome Success Cannot Repair an Invalid Mechanism Trace
outcomeCannotRepairMechanism.meaning: a graph, loop, authority, runtime or mechanism-witness failure is not overridden by a successful outcome
outcomeCannotRepairMechanism.consequence: a load-bearing mechanism failure makes the system invalid regardless of Y

CANONICAL_TRUTH.definition: the canonical project graph: the durable, append-only, hash-chained owner facts
CANONICAL_TRUTH.observedBy: the canonical stores and their read models, addressed by durable identity

RUNTIME_TRUTH.definition: the runtime realization graph: what the shipped runtime actually composed and executed
RUNTIME_TRUTH.observedBy: the runtime payload, the session artifact and the host telemetry

EVIDENCE_TRUTH.definition: the evidence/observation graph: what was recorded about an execution, with digests
EVIDENCE_TRUTH.observedBy: the experimental trace and its digests

BEHAVIORAL_OUTCOME.definition: the behavioral outcome: what a task produced, judged by an acceptance oracle

forbiddenInferences.why: a passing task does not prove the canonical graph is well-formed
a passing task does not prove the runtime realized the intended mechanism
a passing task does not prove the evidence chain is complete
what ran is not what is canonically true

consumerBoundaryLaw.statement: Consumer Boundary Is the Authoritative Observation Boundary

rules.insufficient: producer intent — the host believing it put a body in the payload
rules.required: the actual consumer-visible session: the model-visible prompt and the governed pull response
rules.observationPoint: the durable worker session artifact and the pull response

rules.insufficient: function invocation — the promotion function having been called
rules.required: post-transaction canonical state: the canonical revision and the committed promotion fact
rules.observationPoint: the canonical ledger after the transaction

rules.insufficient: remote fulfillment alone — the peer having delivered something
rules.required: local project state and future use: an explicit local act and a later local Work that consumes it
rules.observationPoint: the local project read model before and after, and the later local Work

rules.insufficient: proposal approval alone — an authority having said yes
rules.required: future Work inheritance: a later attempt actually receiving the revised intent
rules.observationPoint: the requirements delivered to a later attempt

WORK.name: Work lineage
WORK.conceptualPath: Project -> Work -> Attempt -> Result -> Verification -> Promotion -> ProjectWorld

nodes.note: the intent root; projectId scopes every other node
a declared unit of work; the TaskEnvelope carries its policy binding
an attempt is authorized before it may execute
the observed outcome of an attempt, addressed by a durable subject ref
INDEPENDENT of the producing attempt: a separate service judges it
the ONLY path from an attempt result to canonical project state
the canonical world basis a later attempt inherits
per-owner candidate types; there is no single CognitiveCandidate type in the repository
admission is a DECISION record, per owner; it is not called AdmissionDecision
the durable, revisioned capital body
the ONLY thing that makes capital eligible for a project; without it the asset is unreachable

nodes.requiredAuthority: the Context owner revalidates the selection during compilation
nodes.note: selection is a request plus its resolved bindings, not a FutureSelection type

COLLABORATION.name: Collaboration lineage
COLLABORATION.conceptualPath: Project reality/Need ground -> Need -> Commitment -> SovereignRemoteWorkRef -> Fulfillment -> LocalAdoption -> LocalContinuation

nodes.note: the OBSERVED local reality a need must be grounded on. NEED_GROUND_KINDS is exactly [BLOCKED_TASK, FAILED_ATTEMPT], so a need cannot be authored from nothing; the ground is a checkable observation carrying a digest

nodes.requiredAuthority: a need admission decision (NeedAdmissionDecision) plus a currentness assessment of the ground
nodes.note: the candidate and its acceptance receipt are owned by project_collaboration; the DURABLE canonical need is the federation ContactNeed, idempotent on the candidate digest

nodes.requiredAuthority: a durable need AND a prior contact request to the holder
nodes.note: a commitment is a promise; it is NOT work authority over the peer
NO such type exists. The remote peer's Work stays in the peer's own canonical ledger; the local side holds only an opaque peer/attempt ref. This absence is the mechanism, not a gap.

nodes.requiredAuthority: the submitter must be the current authenticated holder
nodes.note: a fulfillment is a delivery claim, NOT an adoption
NO such type exists. Adoption is an explicit local journal entry and, if it becomes work, a local promotion. Fulfillment alone never writes local truth.
NO such type exists in this sense. Continuation is ordinary local Work that the local project owns outright; ResultContinuationService is a DIFFERENT (D5 rework) concept and is not this node.

EVOLUTION.name: Evolution lineage
EVOLUTION.conceptualPath: Observation/Basis -> Proposal -> AuthorityDecision -> RevisionReceipt -> RevisedIntent/Organization/Runtime -> FutureWork

nodes.note: a basis must be a durable, addressable fact; the intent path binds proofs, reasoning and negative results
a proposal is NOT canonical truth; prepare writes nothing

nodes.requiredAuthority: an INDEPENDENT authority port; absent authority must mean UNRESOLVED, never approval
nodes.note: there is no single AuthorityDecision type; each owner has its own outcome union

nodes.requiredAuthority: the accepted admission decision it records (the receipt re-derives its own digest, so it cannot be forged)
nodes.note: no single RevisionReceipt type; the intent receipt is carried on PROJECT_REVISED

nodes.requiredAuthority: the receipt that authorized the revision
nodes.note: the revised intent is a NEW ProjectIr revision, not a RevisedIntent type
the proof of evolution is that a LATER attempt receives the revised intent

durableEventFamilies.consumer: src/state projection then the WorkReadModel read model (src/work/read_model.ts)
durableEventFamilies.retry: append is CAS-guarded by expected head; a conflicting append is REFUSED, not retried blindly
durableEventFamilies.note: every event type in EVENT_TYPES has a strict payload parser, so an unknown or malformed payload is refused at the boundary

durableEventFamilies.consumer: src/context resolveKnowledgeBindings (eligibility) and the workspace read model
durableEventFamilies.retry: appendAtomic is CAS-guarded on the prior chain digest
durableEventFamilies.note: ASSET_ASSOCIATED is the event that makes capital ELIGIBLE; omitting it leaves the asset admitted but unreachable

durableEventFamilies.consumer: src/context proof binding resolution, and the proof asset view
durableEventFamilies.retry: event id is derived from type+scope+payload, so a duplicate append is idempotent
durableEventFamilies.note: the blob store is a directory, so the BYTES survive a restart even though they are not in sqlite

durableEventFamilies.consumer: src/context reasoning binding resolution, and the reasoning frontier read
durableEventFamilies.retry: chain-digest guarded; reasoningChainDigest over the prior event chain
durableEventFamilies.note: admission can later move to INACTIVE; the compile-time binding stays immutable while `current` moves

durableEventFamilies.consumer: the federation read services and durableContactNeedScopeGuard (src/federation/federation_service.ts), which replays history
durableEventFamilies.retry: per-type payload parsers; the scope guard replays history rather than trusting a caller
durableEventFamilies.note: ONE physical store carries BOTH participation and collaboration streams, kept separate by typed parsers

durableEventFamilies.consumer: the fulfillment output admission (a boundary_revision must be an EXACT accepted revision)
durableEventFamilies.note: the accepted-revision set is the authority a fulfillment output is validated against

durableEventFamilies.consumer: the workspace view and promoteOpportunity (src/project_workspace), which turns an OPPORTUNITY into local Work
durableEventFamilies.note: this is the LOCAL ADOPTION act in code; a fulfillment without a journal entry has not been adopted

eventDefectFlags.WRITE_ONLY_EVENT: an event is produced durably but nothing ever consumes or reconciles it
eventDefectFlags.UNCONSUMED_RECEIPT: a receipt is written but no later read observes it
eventDefectFlags.CONSUMER_WITHOUT_OWNER: something consumes a record that has no canonical owner
eventDefectFlags.ORPHANED_RUNTIME_PROJECTION: a runtime projection exists with no canonical owner behind it

systemValidCategories.question: are the canonical lineages well-formed, scoped, owned and receipted?
do the four loops and their cross-loop seams hold on every exercised load-bearing path?
does the shipped runtime realize the configured mechanism, with the experimental flags off?
is every authority-bearing write preceded by an independent decision?
does every conformance run record digests sufficient to re-establish what was tested?
are the known prohibited bypasses blocked, and do mutations get detected?

notApplicable.reason: the knowledge stores are append-only with CAS-guarded writes; a crash mid-append is covered by the store suites, not by this loop matrix
the coordination store is append-only and the federation services re-derive from history; a crash mid-append is a store concern
the revision is one canonical append, so a crash either committed it or did not; the stale path already covers the move between prepare and apply

crossLoopScenarios.statement: a completed/verified project outcome becomes admitted durable capital and is consumable by a later cold-started attempt
a remote fulfillment affects future local cognition only after explicit local adoption
a governed revision actually changes future work inputs

preregisteredMutations.description: drop the worker contextIndexText, so the model-visible prompt loses the index
preregisteredMutations.seam: the worker port boundary in the test harness

preregisteredMutations.description: remove or bypass the per-attempt handle allowlist, so any handle resolves
preregisteredMutations.seam: the pull resolver the host binds to the attempt

preregisteredMutations.description: attempt promotion without a successful independent verification
accept a stale result where optimistic concurrency should reject or continue
omit the ProjectAssetAssociation after asset admission, so the capital is unreachable
preregisteredMutations.seam: the association store the harness injects

preregisteredMutations.description: write an evolution receipt but feed the OLD intent to future Work
preregisteredMutations.seam: the intent port that supplies requirement statements to a later attempt

historicalDefects.description: the worker index was not forwarded to the model-visible prompt, so a selected body never reached the consumer
historicalDefects.how: the proof reads the model-visible session and fails when the index/body is absent, instead of trusting that the producer put it in the payload

historicalDefects.description: a gate whose assertion was written so it could never fail (the literal unconditional form)
historicalDefects.how: the anti-vacuity scanner forbids the unconditional literal form in gate code, and this stage keeps its gates under a scanned directory

historicalDefects.description: the qualification engine read trial[classId] instead of trial.classPass[classId], so every class collapsed into one group
historicalDefects.how: the engine is driven with REAL nested records end to end, and the analysis must reproduce from the preserved trials

bypassChecks.question: can a consumer read the backing store directly, bypassing the governed channel?
can a consumer resolve a handle that was never compiled into its attempt?
can a consumer use another attempt's identity or context?
can a worker reach the host control payload where that is prohibited?
can a write land without its required authority decision?
can a remote fulfillment become local canonical truth without an explicit local act?

bypassClaim.reason: the checks enumerate known bypasses and block them; they are not a proof about unknown ones

mechanismWitnessChain.question: what canonical fact had to be true before the mechanism could act?
what did the runtime actually compose from it?
what did the CONSUMER actually see, at the boundary?
which action/tool was the consumer permitted to use?
what durable fact resulted, addressable after a restart?

taskSuccessWithoutWitness.ruling: this is NOT mechanism success, and it may not support a mechanism claim
